title: Working from home
prompt: Why do many people now prefer to work from home rather than in an office? Should employers allow all staff to work remotely?

sentences.text: Remote working has become common in many sectors, and it is now a central question for managers planning the future of their organisations.
sentences.why: Neutral background that places the topic in a managerial context. "Central question for managers" frames the second question without answering it, and "remote working" is a natural paraphrase, supporting Lexical Resource.

sentences.text: People value remote work mainly for its flexibility and lower costs, but I believe employers should not allow every employee to work from home by default.
sentences.why: A thesis that answers both questions in one sentence. "Mainly for its flexibility and lower costs" answers Question 1 and "should not allow every employee" answers Question 2, meeting Task Response fully with a clear stance.

sentences.text: This essay will explain the main reasons for the preference and then assess whether a blanket policy is sensible.
sentences.why: The outline separates the two questions in order using "first" and "then assess". It promises a full answer to both parts, supporting Coherence and Cohesion, and "blanket policy" is an apt noun phrase.

sentences.text: The first reason people prefer home working is the flexibility it offers, particularly for those with caring responsibilities.
sentences.why: A topic sentence for Question 1 that names the main reason and a specific group, "caring responsibilities". "The first reason" signals sequence, and the noun phrase is precise, supporting Task Response and Lexical Resource.

sentences.text: Being able to start and finish work at suitable times, without a daily commute, allows employees to balance professional and family demands more easily.
sentences.why: Explains the mechanism with "without a daily commute" as a clear causal step. The gerund subject "Being able to" and the verb "balance" show grammatical range, and the clause links flexibility to family demands logically.

sentences.text: A parent who collects a child from school, for instance, may be able to complete the working day without an exhausting journey.
sentences.why: A concrete example centred on one person: "a parent who collects a child". The relative clause and "exhausting journey" make it vivid, and "may be able" is a sensible hedge, giving credible development.

sentences.text: This flexibility can reduce stress and improve job satisfaction, which in turn helps retain experienced staff.
sentences.why: The effect sentence moves from stress to satisfaction to retention, with "which in turn" showing the chain. It converts a personal example into an organisational benefit relevant to employers, supporting Task Response.

sentences.text: However, a policy that allows every employee to work remotely would overlook important differences between jobs and individuals.
sentences.why: A contrast topic sentence for Question 2: "However" turns the argument, and "overlook important differences" explains why a blanket rule is flawed. The conditional "would" suits a hypothetical policy.

sentences.text: Some roles, such as nursing, manufacturing and retail, require a physical presence, while newer staff often benefit from being in an office to learn from colleagues.
sentences.why: Lists job types that require presence (nursing, manufacturing, retail) and then adds a contrasting group, newer staff, with "while". This gives two distinct reasons within one explanation, showing breadth and range.

sentences.text: A junior analyst who works only from home, for example, may find it harder to build the informal relationships that lead to promotion.
sentences.why: The example is a "junior analyst" who misses informal relationships, which is specific and ties to promotion. "Only from home" is a precise condition, and the example directly supports the claim about newer staff.

sentences.text: Therefore, a flexible system based on individual needs and job roles would be fairer than a universal rule.
sentences.why: The link sentence draws the conclusion from the example: "Therefore" marks the logical result and "fairer" is an evaluative adjective. It proposes a flexible alternative, which shows judgement and supports Task Response.

sentences.text: In summary, home working offers real advantages in flexibility and wellbeing, but these benefits depend on the nature of the job and the employee.
sentences.why: The conclusion restates both answers in new words: "real advantages" for Question 1, and "depend on the nature of the job" for Question 2. It matches the thesis and keeps the position consistent.

sentences.text: Employers should therefore allow remote work where it suits both the role and the team, rather than adopting a single policy for everyone.
sentences.why: A final recommendation answering "should" with a qualified yes: "where it suits both the role and the team". It contrasts with "a single policy", closing on the limit of universal rules without new ideas.

analysis: There are two separate questions: "Why do many people now prefer to work from home?" (a reasons question) and "Should employers allow all staff to work remotely?" (a judgement question). Each needs its own paragraph.
Question 2 contains "all staff", which limits the claim. A strong answer notices that "all" is the key word and responds to it directly instead of discussing remote work in general.

Paraphrase in the introduction: "work from home" becomes remote working or home-based work; "rather than in an office" becomes instead of commuting to a workplace; "employers allow all staff" becomes a blanket remote policy.

Position: people prefer home working for flexibility and lower costs, but a universal policy is unwise. The two answers fit together, since the reasons for preference depend on personal circumstances and job type.
The question does not ask for advantages and disadvantages of remote work in general, or for a history of the trend. Avoid drifting into both-sides discussion.
Give both parts roughly equal space, and use one example per paragraph: a parent for Question 1 and a junior analyst for Question 2.

plan.idea: Remote work is now common. Thesis: people value flexibility and lower costs, but employers should not allow every employee to work from home by default.
Why: flexibility, especially for carers, without a commute. Example: a parent collecting a child from school. Result: lower stress, higher job satisfaction, better retention of experienced staff.

Should: not for all staff. Nursing, manufacturing and retail need presence; newer staff learn in offices. Example: a junior analyst missing informal relationships. Link: a flexible system by role is fairer.
Home working has real advantages for flexibility and wellbeing, but these depend on the job; employers should allow it where it suits role and team.
